summary: Zileuton is an oral 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor for prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma in adults and children 12 years and older. The extended-release dose is 1200 mg (two 600 mg tablets) twice daily within one hour after morning and evening meals (total 2400 mg/day); immediate-release is 600 mg four times daily. Because of hepatotoxicity, serum ALT must be monitored: at baseline, monthly for 3 months, every 2-3 months for the rest of the first year, then periodically. It is not for acute bronchospasm.
indications: Prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma in adults and children 12 years of age and older

dosage.d: 1200 mg (two 600 mg ER tablets) twice daily, total 2400 mg/day
dosage.n: Take within 1 hour after morning and evening meals

dosage.d: 600 mg four times daily, total 2400 mg/day
dosage.n: Includes a dose with meals and at bedtime

dosage.d: Check serum ALT before therapy and per schedule; discontinue if ALT >=5x ULN or signs of liver dysfunction
dosage.n: Baseline, monthly x3, then every 2-3 months

admin: Extended-release tablets are swallowed whole within one hour after the morning and evening meals; do not crush or chew
Use regularly for chronic asthma control; not for relief of acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus
Obtain a baseline serum ALT before starting therapy
Monitor ALT monthly for the first 3 months, every 2-3 months for the remainder of the first year, then periodically
Discontinue and follow transaminases if ALT rises >=5x the upper limit of normal or liver dysfunction develops
moa: Zileuton is a specific inhibitor of 5-lipoxygenase, the enzyme that catalyzes the first step in the conversion of arachidonic acid to leukotrienes (LTB4, LTC4, LTD4 and LTE4). By blocking leukotriene synthesis it reduces leukotriene-mediated bronchoconstriction, airway edema, mucus secretion, vascular permeability and recruitment of eosinophils and neutrophils, attenuating the inflammatory component of asthma.

absolute: Persistent serum transaminase elevations >=3x the upper limit of normal
Hypersensitivity to zileuton or any component
relative: History of liver disease or heavy alcohol use
Patients unwilling or unable to undergo ALT monitoring

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Animal studies showed reduced fetal/pup survival at high doses. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether zileuton is excreted in human milk; it is found in rat milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, a decision should be made to discontinue nursing or the drug.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment; zileuton is cleared mainly by hepatic metabolism with renal excretion of metabolites. It is not removed by hemodialysis.
hepatic: Contraindicated in active liver disease or persistent ALT elevations >=3x ULN. Zileuton can cause elevated hepatic transaminases (ALT >=3x ULN in about 2.5% in 12-week trials), so liver enzymes must be monitored and the drug stopped for significant elevations or symptoms.

major: Theophylline - zileuton roughly doubles theophylline levels (clearance reduced ~50%); halve theophylline dose and monitor levels
Warfarin - increases warfarin (R-isomer) exposure; monitor prothrombin time/INR and adjust dose
moderate: Propranolol - increased propranolol exposure (~beta-blocker effect); monitor and reduce dose as needed
Other CYP1A2/2C9/3A4 substrates - zileuton may alter their metabolism
minor: Other potentially hepatotoxic drugs - additive liver risk
interactions.food: Extended-release taken within 1 hour after meals; food modestly affects ER absorption.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate serum ALT/AST; monitor liver enzymes per schedule.

serious: Behavioral and mood-related changes (sleep disorders, depression, agitation)

monitoring: Serum ALT: baseline, monthly for first 3 months, every 2-3 months for the rest of the first year, then periodically
Clinical signs and symptoms of liver dysfunction (RUQ pain, jaundice, fatigue, pruritus)
Theophylline levels and INR (warfarin) when co-administered
counsel: Take extended-release tablets within 1 hour after your morning and evening meals; swallow whole
Keep all liver blood-test appointments - this drug can affect the liver
Stop and contact your doctor if you have right-sided belly pain, nausea, tiredness, itching, dark urine or yellowing of skin/eyes
This is a controller, not a rescue medicine - keep using your inhaler for sudden symptoms
Report mood changes, agitation, sleep problems or thoughts of self-harm; avoid alcohol
pk: Days for asthma control; not for acute relief
Plasma peak ~1.7 h (IR); steady-state Cmax ~4.9 mcg/mL (ER)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions 15-30 C permitted
pearls: Hepatotoxicity is the defining risk - mandatory scheduled ALT monitoring (baseline, monthly x3, then q2-3 months); contraindicated with active liver disease or ALT >=3x ULN
Doubles theophylline levels - halve the theophylline dose and monitor
Also raises warfarin and propranolol exposure - monitor INR and beta-blocker effect
5-lipoxygenase inhibitor - blocks leukotriene synthesis upstream of the LTRAs (montelukast/zafirlukast)
Not a rescue medication - controller therapy only
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up. Maintaining consistent dosing is important for asthma control.
overdose: Human overdose experience is limited; zileuton was well tolerated at high single doses in studies. Zileuton is not dialyzable. In overdose, induce emesis or perform gastric lavage if appropriate, provide supportive and symptomatic care, and monitor liver enzymes and vital signs.
